title: Restriction augmentation for one injective étale sheaf on an open cover
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let i:X.Opens → X.Etale be cover preserving and preserve finite limits, and suppose i(top) is terminal [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let U be a finite u-small open covering of X. For any injective étale abelian sheaf J valued in AddCommGrpCat of universe u+1 [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], every map e from J(i(top)) concentrated in cochain degree zero to Cech(U,i^*J) [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex], whose degree-zero projections are restriction along i of the inclusions of tuple intersections into top, is a quasi-isomorphism. No resolution, total complex, or derived evaluation occurs in this assertion. Empty covers are allowed.

source.place: Lemma 21.10.2, including its degree-zero clause; Tag 03F6; row comparison in lem-sc-etale-open-cech-resolution-total, steps 1 and 2

proof.text: The open covering defines a covering sieve on top. Cover preservation pushes it to a covering sieve on i(top). Since i preserves finite limits and i(top) is terminal, i applied to a finite open product is a product of the image opens, equivalently their fibre product over i(top). The unique projection-compatible product isomorphisms commute with each omitted-factor map, so restriction along them identifies the alternating Cech complexes. Reindex the open family using ULift into universe u+1 when invoking the large-index etale acyclicity interface; the equivalence of tuple index types induces inverse product maps commuting with each differential.

Apply injective_sheaf_cech_acyclic to the image covering and J. Transport the vanishing back through the projection-compatible complex isomorphism to obtain zero positive homology of Cech(U,i^*J). The single-term source has zero homology in positive degrees, so the induced maps there are isomorphisms between zero objects.

In degree zero the differential says exactly that the restrictions to pairwise intersections agree. Apply the sheaf condition on the image covering: there is a unique section at i(top) giving any such compatible family. This is additive and its inverse is the canonical restriction map fixed by he. There is no incoming differential in degree zero, so this identifies the homology map of e with an isomorphism. The same sheaf condition forces sections to be zero for an empty cover, and the Cech terms are empty products, hence zero objects. Thus e is a quasi-isomorphism in all degrees.
